In the equivalent circuit, the motional resistance R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> and the motional inductance L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> were increased, but the motional capacitance C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> and the capacitance C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> were decreased with the increasing of overtone mode order.

articleTitle: Fabrication of fine-scaled PZT/epoxy composites for medical imaging applications
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: This paper mainly focused on the processing issues for fabricating fine-scaled PZT/epoxy composites for ultrasonic medical imaging applications. Tape casting technique was utilized for fabricating ceramic and carbon black tapes. The effects of the solid loading on the density of the sintered PZT ceramic wafers were discussed. A 2-2 composite with average PZT element width of 35μm was fabricated and characterized. The PZT volume fraction was ~50%. The k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> was calculated to be 0.62.

articleTitle: Abnormal environment experiment research of linear ultrasonic motor
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: To do research on the influence of three factors, such as the preload, the ambient pressure and the ambient temperature, on the V type Linear ultrasonic motor (V-LUSM), this study does experiments by using V-LUSM in abnormal environment. This study sets the preload as the main factor, meanwhile considering the influence of ambient pressure and temperature. In the experiments, the study measures the moment of force and the velocity of V-LUSM in different environment made up of different preload, pressure and temperature. Comparing all datum partitioned by those three factors above, the study can conclude that V-LUSM can work in the abnormal environment. The performance of V-LUSM is affected more by preload, and less by ambient pressure and temperature.

articleTitle: Optimal cut of quartz for a surface acoustic wave pressure sensor with non-uniform pressure load
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: This paper aimed to study the pressure sensitive coefficients of different cuts of quartz for the surface acoustic wave(SAW) pressure sensors with non-uniform pressure load, and tried to find the most sensitive cut. The finite element analysis/ perturbation theory combines model was constructed to calculate the pressure sensitive coefficients. For analysis of different cut angles (0, θ, φ) of quartz with φ (0~180°), θ (-90~90°), the optimal cuts angle of quartz(0°, 4.5°, 64.7°) was found.

articleTitle: A new trapped mode caused by local defect or thermal inhomogeneity
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: The trapped modes, widely used in resonators, filters, quartz crystal microbalance, and other wave devices, are usually excited by attaching a partially mass layer or electrode on the surface of a plate. A new thickness-twist trapped mode in a transversely piezoelectric plate with a defect or local inhomogeneous temperature in it has been obtained by using of power series expansion method. Numerical results obtained indicate that trapped modes exist in such a damaged or thermal plate, which can not be observed when the plate is homogeneous. The finding of energy trapping phenomenon provides a new style for the excitation of trapped waves.

articleTitle: Finite difference numerical simulations of acoustic fields using the graphic processing unit
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: The finite difference time domain (FDTD) method is widely used in numerical simulations of acoustic fields. When the size of the model is too large, the amount of the grid points in the computational region is correspondingly huge, then the simulation will cost a lot of calculation time using CPU in a serial program. In this paper we use the graphic processing unit (GPU) to solve this problem. First, we use GPU to accelerate the numerical simulation of 2D second-order FDTD for the fluid medium model and get a 50-time speedup. Then we accelerate a 3-D model in horizontally layered isotropic medium and obtain a 10-time speedup. Based on this research, we can use GPU to accelerate simulations of more complicated models with MPI or OpenMP.

articleTitle: A broadband piezoelectric energy harvester regulated by light activated shape memory polymer
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid energy harvesting system is established and studied; the natural frequency of which is regulated by a novel intelligent material named light activated shape memory polymer (LaSMP). LaSMP realizes the shape memory function under the exposure of laser lights with two different wavelengths. During the exposure process, LaSMP exhibits a characteristic of dynamic stiffening effect. A cantilever beam laminated with LaSMP and piezoelectric layers is used as a broadband hybrid energy harvester. Employing this stiffening characteristic of the LaSMP, the natural frequency of the hybrid energy harvester can be manipulated to achieve broadband energy harvesting response. The hybrid energy harvester is designed to adjust its frequency to resonance at the excitation frequency. The results show that the natural frequency of the hybrid energy harvester can be tuned by 5.2%, and the minimum energy harvesting power output increases from 0.001uW to 0.01μW.

articleTitle: Separation of small solid particles based on ultrasonic rotation
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: In this work, we proposed and developed an ultrasonic actuator which can be used to separate mixed small solid particles in air. The ultrasonic actuator consists of an ultrasonic sandwich-type transducer and an aluminum plate which is extended from an end plate of the transducer. The aluminum plate is asymmetrically excited by the transducer, to vibrate flexurally. The transducer operates in the thickness mode and has a resonance frequency of 91.7 kHz. Particle mixtures used in the experiments are obtained by the combination of any two particles among shrimp eggs, glass balls and refined salt. The experiments show that the glass balls can be separated from the mixture of glass balls and shrimp eggs, and salt particles separated from the mixture of salt particles and shrimp eggs. The device used in the method has no mechanical rotary part and the separation can be quickly completed.

articleTitle: PSPICE analyses of vibration energy harvester systems with multiple piezoelectric components
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: In this letter, a PSPICE based simulation is conducted to analyze the system of a vibration energy harvester with multiple piezoelectric components and the basic energy storage circuit. By the simulation, the optimal capacitance of the storage capacitor is determined to obtain a maximum energy storage power, and the effect of circuit parameters of the piezoelectric components on the stored energy is clarified.

articleTitle: The study of P-SV wave propagation in the periodic piezoelectric layered material
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: The piezoelectric material is playing a more and more important role in the active control of the wave propagation, and is introduced into the one-dimensional phononic crystal for the actively wave control. In this paper, the P-SV wave propagation in the periodic piezoelectric layered material is studied, a model of the problem is established, and the wave propagation is simulated by the COMSOL multi-physics software. The relationship between the transmission coefficients and the incident angle under the different electrical boundary conditions are obtained numerically; meanwhile the results are compared to those obtained by the softness matrix method. And the analytical and numerical results agree quite well for the electric circuit open or closed piezoelectric material and the piezoelectricity ignored material. The influence of the electric boundary condition on the P-SV wave propagation in the periodic piezoelectric layered material is obtained, The acoustic field and electric field distribution are also obtained by the numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Study on resonant frequency and impedance properties of film bulk acoustic resonator
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: Based on the fundamental piezoelastic theory, the vibration equation of layered FBAR under sine excitation voltage was derived. The unknown constants were calculated with boundary and continuity conditions. The expressions of electrical impedance were obtained from the electrical potential and current. The series and parallel resonance frequency are then calculated when the electrical impedance tends to infinite and zero. The bandwidth and effective electromechanical coupling factor are calculated from the series and parallel resonance frequency. The Bragg reflection layers will reduce the loss of mechanical energy.

articleTitle: Researches on the vibration characteristics of a new type of non-resonant piezoelectric stack motors
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: To research on the mechanism of non-resonant linear piezoelectric motors, longitudinal vibration model and pseudo-rigid-body model were established for the stator of motor through the analysis of the construction and operating process of the motor. Then the longitudinal vibration differential equation and transverse vibration differential equation of the drive tip were produced. Thus longitudinal displacement function and transverse displacement function can be deduced. Utilizing the above researches, formula of average output force in a period was proposed for the motor. Finally, the prototype was designed and fabricated, vibration displacement is tested by laser displacement sensor and vibration displacement curves were fitted through origin software. Thus experiments on the longitudinal amplitude of drive tip were carried on. The output force of motor under different excitation conditions were measured with force measurement unit. Results proved the vibration characteristic theory of stator that the longitudinal amplitude of drive tip increases with excitation voltage and that the output force of motor increases with the longitudinal amplitude of drive tip. The output force prototype can be up to 3.5 N when the longitude amplitude of the stator is 0.95μm. The above researches can provide theoretical basis for structural optimization for the stator of motor.

articleTitle: The study of aging frequency drift mechanism for quartz crystal resonators
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: Aging as long-term stability is one of the most important characteristics of quartz crystal resonators, and stress and out-gas make major contributions. In this paper, aging frequency drift mechanisms under different conditions of mounting types and aging temperatures are analyzed. The results show that the frequency drift under 85°C aging of both two-point and four-point mounted quartz chip are similar; however, the stability performance under 150°C aging of two-point mounted resonator is much better than that of four-point mounted ones. The main reason is the aging curve of two-point mounted resonator is a comprehensive aging curve, since effects of out-gas and stress are balanced well, which is supported by the I VA test.

articleTitle: Axisymmetric wave propagation along the piezoelectric composite cylinder with mechanically imperfect interface
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: Based on linear piezoelectric and elastic theory, axisymmetric wave propagation along the piezoelectric layered composite cylinder is analyzed and the dispersion equation is derived by subjecting general solutions to specific boundary and continuity conditions. The existence of both axial and radial interfacial imperfections is considered using a linear spring model. It is found that the behaviors of dispersion curves are quite different due to different interfacial imperfections. Effect of ratio of inner to outer radius is also investigated. Mode shapes under different interfacial imperfections are discussed and it is found that mode shapes are sensitive to small interfacial parameters.

articleTitle: Transport AC loss of a cylindrical superconducting composite based on the Kim model
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: The transport ac loss for a superconducting composite cylinder, which consists of two concentric shells with different critical current densities, is calculated in the presence of transport current. First, the nonlinear equations and the corresponding boundary conditions for the magnetic field distributions are given for increasing transport current by adopting the Kim model. Then, the integral expression of transport ac loss is derived based on the Norris equations. Finally, some typical numerical results for the ac loss are plotted graphically and analyzed in detail. The numerical results show that, among others, both the superconducting parameters of the Kim model including the outer and inner shells and the ratio of the inside and outside radii have significant and different effects on the transport ac loss.

articleTitle: An analytic study for a rotating FGPM hollow
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: An analytic solution to the axisymmetric problem of a long, radially polarized, functionally graded piezoelectric material (FGPM) hollow cylinder rotating about its axis at a constant angular velocity is presented. For the case that electric, thermal and mechanical properties of the material obey different power laws in the thickness direction, distributions for radial displacement, stresses and electric potential in the FGPM hollow cylinder are determined by using the theory of electro-thermoelasticity Some useful discussions and numerical examples are presented to show the significant influence of material nonhomogeneity, and adopting suitable graded indexes and applying suitable geometric size and rotating velocity ω may optimize the rotating FGPM hollow cylindrical structures.

articleTitle: Horizontal shear surface waves in a functionally graded piezoelectric cylinder
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: Horizontal shear (SH) surface acoustic wave propagation is evaluated in a transversely isotropic functionally graded piezoelectric material (FGPM) cylinder with material parameters varying continuously along the radial direction. The power series method is used to solve the coupled governing equations with variable coefficients. We discuss the influence of gradient property of each material parameter on the phase velocities. The phase velocities for the electric open circuit are illustrated and the influences of the gradient coefficient of FGPM on the phase velocities are quantified. Results provide theoretical guidance not only for experimental measurement of material properties but also for nondestructive evaluation using the ultrasonic wave devices.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of the interaction of Rayleigh wave to the sub-surface cracks
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: The interaction of ultrasonic waves with cracks is analyzed numerically in this paper. The nonlinear effect due to the asymmetric stiffness called contact acoustic nonlinearity (CAN) is focused. Longitudinal wave and Raleigh wave are excited separately to investigate their nonlinear interaction with cracks. Numerical results demonstrate that super-harmonics and sub-harmonics can be generated, and frequency of Rayleigh wave only in certain range can excite the harmonics when has some relations with depth of crack.

articleTitle: Stress analysis of electrostrictive material with two circular holes
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: Based on the complex variable method, we analyzed the two-dimensional problems of an electrostrictive solid with two circular holes. The solid is subjected to electric field at infinity. The complex potentials of electric and electroelastic fields were first expressed by introducing series expansion with unknown coefficients. Then, using the boundary condition, we can calculate the unknown coefficients, and so all the complex potentials were derived. Numerical examples are presented to study the influence of the distance and angle between two holes on the stress distribution around the hole, and discussions are also made about the effect of the electric fields in the hole on the stress field.

articleTitle: Design of passive wireless interface module reactance sensor based on Surface Acoustic Wave
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: Based on Surface Acoustic Wave Resonator (SAWR), the SAWR equivalent circuit is built, and its model is established, so the circuit parameters of SAWR are obtained by S11 of Vector Network Analyzer (VNA). Furthermore, taking the T type for example, the values of interface matching element are calculated based on self-adaptation matching theory. The processes of actual matching verify the validity of theoretical matching research, and finding the matching difference between the actual value and the calculation value. Then single ended interface module is designed, tested, wired and wireless analyzed, sensor analysis, the results of which show the validity of single ended interface module and give a scheme of Pi-CLC double ended interface module based on linearity and sensitivity. Finally, double ended interface module is also packaged, wired and wireless test proves the validity of it, the difference frequency analysis shows that reference resonator not affect the main resonator to dominant the difference frequency changing with capacitance sensor and SWR analysis shows the design validity of low mismatching network.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of laser excited 3D acoustic field of semi-infinite isotropic solid
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: Laser ultrasonic technique is an advanced development of the traditional ultrasound technique. Compared to the traditional ultrasonic technique, it has advantages such as non-contact detection. In this paper, an isotropic semi-infinite solid is employed as the theoretical model to analyze the acoustic field generated by the laser pulse. The differential equations are solved with 3D Fourier transform and then 3D inverse fast Fourier transform is used to obtain the displacement field. On the other hand, the model for the finite element simulation should be an aluminum plate with larger thickness. The laser pulse is simplified as a normal force. In both calculation and simulation, it can be observed that laser excited ultrasounds will propagate along the surface of the specimen and inside the specimen. This work has laid out the theoretic foundation for the analytic solution of the 3D acoustic field of a semi-infinite isotropic solid with defects. Based on the finite element simulation of the laser excited acoustic field for the specimen with or without defects, the inverse problem is going to be carried out to determine the size and location of a certain crack.

articleTitle: The research of the clamping effect on the linear ultrasonic motors
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: The flexible hinge has been proved to be more suitable for the clamping design than the spring. But, it still lacks in-depth research on how the flexible hinge affects the motor's output. In this paper, the laser interferometer is used to measure the real-time displacement of the slide, from which the speed and acceleration curves can be compared to research on this question. Ultimately, the maximum output speed of motors is respectively 570mm/s, 480mm/s, 360mm/s, and the maximum output force of 12N, 16N, 18N. The results show that the linear ultrasonic motors with larger transverse stiffness will get lower speed but larger force output, whose output will also be more stable.

articleTitle: Self-validating passive wireless SAW sensor
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: The surface acoustic wave (SAW) sensors are very suit for the applications under harsh environmental conditions, which cause temporal failures, signal shadowing, multi-path fading and signal attenuation pose great challenges in the reliability of passive wireless SAW sensor. This paper proposes a method to evaluate measurement uncertainty before operating frequency measurement, deduce the relationship between the measurement uncertainty of resonant SAW sensor and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), which is based on the Fisher information matrix and subspace parameters. This estimator can be further used to identify and skip the faulty conditions. The proposed approach is evaluated in simulations and practical experiments.

articleTitle: Research on a double-foot driving linear piezoelectric motor
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: In order to develop high precision, large travel, heavy thrust linear piezoelectric motor, a marching type linear piezoelectric motor based on the piezoelectric stack was proposed. The operating principle of the motor was presented, the structure of the motor was designed, a prototype was made and the experimental studies were carried through. The experimental results showed that within a certain range of frequency the amplitude of the motor's stator driving foot was linear to the driving voltage, and the maximum amplitude was 2.9 μm. The maximum non-load velocity of the motor was 796 μm/s, the maximum output thrust of the motor was 4.8 N. The expected design objective has been successfully obtained.

articleTitle: Effect of zirconium content on the property of BCTZ lead-free piezoelectric ceramics
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: Ba<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.85</sub>Ca<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</sub>Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-y</sub>Zr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (BCTZ) (y =0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.2) lead-free piezoelectric ceramics were prepared by conventional solid state method. Effects of Zr content on the piezoelectric and dielectric properties and microstructure of BCTZ lead-free piezoelectric ceramics were investigated. The results show that the average crystal grain size of BCTZ increases gradually, the crystal grain uniformity goes down; all the samples exhibit a pure perovskite structure and no trace of impurity phase was observed. The piezoelectric constant(d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</sub>), the planar electromechanical coupling factor (k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>) of BCTZ ceramics increases first and then decreases, the relative permittivity (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>) increases gradually, the dielectric loss (tanδ) increases first and then decreases when Zr content increases. When Zr content (y) is 0.10, the BCTZ ceramics sintered at 1450, possess the best piezoelectric properties and dielectric properties whose d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">33</sub> is 424pC/N, k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> is 48.83%,ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> is 4364, tanδ is 1.12%.

articleTitle: Crack detection in a framed structure using PCA-compressed piezoelectric signatures
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: In order to overcome the current problems of the transmission and storage of the measured data in the structural health monitoring system, it was necessary to put forward the compression sensing method to the neural network system and electro-mechanical impedance (EMI) technology. The finite element EMI model was first established for a framed structure and the conductance data were accordingly obtained for various crack severities. The compressed data by compression sensing theory were used to depict the structural damages instead of the raw ones, and were further investigated using the principal component analysis (PCA). The obtained principal components (PCs) were then used to be the input parameters of the BP artificial neural network (ANN). Results showed that the transmission bandwidth and storage space of the EMI data were only 16% of the original ones using the compression perception theory. The neural network system could detect the existence of cracks and could further classify the crack severities quantitatively using the principal components of the compressed conductance.

articleTitle: Dynamics modeling of piezoelectric control for the aircraft wings in aerodynamic thermal environment
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: In this paper, the aircraft wings are simplified as the cantilever beam structure. Piezoelectric actuator is used to eliminate the effects in the thermal environment. Mathematical modeling of cantilever beam in the temperature field are built. Simulation of the accessional control by piezoelectric film model show the feasibility of the control method preliminarily. And our purpose is enhance the performance of the structures on the base of general materials by using smart material and effective control methods in the future.

articleTitle: The acoustic theory to measure the volume fraction of suspended particul ate matter in the air
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: Suspended particles are a general term for solid and the liquid particulate matter suspended in the atmosphere. Total suspended particles in air quality evaluation are an important general pollution index. This paper aims to find a simple acoustic method to measure the volume of the total suspended particles. In order to measure the volume fraction of suspended particulate matter in the air, we studied the effect of the volume fraction and the density of the suspended particulate matter on the speed of the sound wave in the air. We considered the suspended particulate matter to the vibration model of the air, and get the equivalent sound velocity by solving the equation of the mass conservation and the energy conservation of the air element when they are vibrating. We found that, the sound speed of the mixture will be affected by the density and the volume fraction of the suspended particulate matter, it will decrease with increasing the particle density when ones keep the volume fraction constant, and so does the volume fraction when ones keep the particle density constant. So we think that, in a certain range of error, the volume fraction of the suspended particulate matter can be determined by measuring the sound velocity in the mixture of the solid particles and air.

articleTitle: Thermal response analysis of variable stiffness of piezoelectric cylindrical shell
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: Materials and structures been unpredictable changed by sudden changes in temperature, alternation temperature and local temperature. The temperature change in structures' surface may coursed by air friction or sunlight illumination in the aerospace environment. In this paper, modal analysis of cylindrical shell by ANSYS is proposed. Static force which been saw as the PZT patches' acting force is added to the cylindrical shell's internal surface. The frequency will be changed by the aeroheating environment and the force. And in this paper, a method to adding force to restore the frequency is proposed.

articleTitle: The active variable stiffness control of cantilever beam by SMA under temperature field
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: This paper is to investigate the active variable stiffness control of cantilever beam under temperature field. Generic system equations of cantilever beam including all constitutive relations are defined. A cantilever beam structure under the temperature fields was modeled. Several control methods with SMA to compensate the influence of thermal stress are proposed, simulated and compared.

articleTitle: Flaw recognition by target matching method
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: Based on the maximum output signal-to-noise ratio criterion, we proposed a target-matching method for flaw recognition in ultrasonic testing. The characteristic of a target flaw is used as a prior knowledge. So the output response can be a self-correlative process with the maximum SNR. The new method is verified by a series of experiments for 5 small typical flaws, including the flat-bottom hole, the narrow-slot crack, the ribbon crack, the internal crack, and the side-drilled hole. the results perform much better testing sensitivity than those in the conventional detection.

articleTitle: A fluid energy driven piezoelectric generator
publicationTitle: 2013 Symposium on Piezoelectricity, Acoustic Waves, and Device Applications
abstract: This study demonstrates a novel fluid energy driven piezoelectric generator with simple structure for generating the electrical power from fluid energy, such as wind energy or water energy. The key components generating the electrical energy in the fluid energy driven generator are series of fixed-fixed piezoelectric composite beam. Potentially, because all the fixed-fixed piezoelectric composite beams in one generator are in phase with each other, the output voltage of the generator can be magnified. The distributed electromechanical model of the generator is derived and the steady state response is obtained. The theoretical results are compared with the FEA simulation results, both agree well with each other.

abstract: The following topics are dealt with: linear ultrasonic motors; solar panel cleaning system; linear piezoelectric actuator; double-foot driving linear piezoelectric motor; single disc piezoelectric ceramic transformer; piezoelectric circular plate actuator; vibration energy harvester; piezoelectric energy harvesting circuit; piezoelectric generator; bulk acoustic wave resonators; wireless energy transmission; valve-less piezoelectric pump; piezoelectric rotational speed meter; passive wireless interface module reactance sensor; SAW reader receiving circuit; double-excited piezoelectric Tonpilz transducer; SAW passive wireless temperature sensor; surface acoustic wave pressure sensor; Love-wave aptasensors; piezoelectric plate transformer; thin film bulk acoustic resonator; non-resonant piezoelectric stack motors; needle-type ultrasonic hydrophone; traveling wave type rotary ultrasonic motor; piezoelectric boundary acoustic wave resonator; flexible magnetoelectric torque unimorph device; underwater acoustic velocity gradient sensors; piezoelectric ring energy harvester; and quartz crystal tuning fork resonator.
